stories.title: Understanding Jensen Huang's AI optimism and how it influences President Trump
stories.summary: The Nvidia CEO is a relentless AI optimist with the president's ear. Stephen Witt, author of The Thinking Machine, tells NPR's Juana Summers how their relationship could shape the future of AI.

stories.title: As Congress confronts AI, Senate lawmakers are shut off from its most advanced tools
stories.summary: While Senate offices have access to chatbots like ChatGPT, they are not authorized to use any of the more advanced tools that are at the center of regulatory talks and public debate about AI safety.

stories.title: Judge appears skeptical of White House ban on CNN, MS NOW and Politico
stories.summary: We get the latest in the court battle between major news outlets and the Trump administration that revoked their access to the White House.

stories.title: FBI records point to possible congressional pay-for-play scheme
stories.summary: NPR's Juana Summers talks with Avi Asher-Schapiro of ProPublica about the connections between a defense contractor and Sen. Susan Collins of Maine, and how the FBI was, at one time, looking into it.

stories.title: What painter Sliman Mansour told NPR about Palestinian rights and art before he died
stories.summary: Born a year before Israel's creation, Palestinian artist Sliman Mansour spent his life painting the faces and landscapes of Israeli occupation. He died in August aged 79, and was buried in the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: How the NPR College Podcast Challenge changed lives
stories.summary: Five years later, the first-ever winner of the NPR College Podcast Challenge looks back at her early work in journalism and talks to other participants about where their stories have taken them.
